title: Estimated cumulative hip bone loss: ISS mission vs a Mars mission, unmitigated
time_coverage: 6-month ISS mission vs ~30-month Mars round trip

source.name: NASA Human Research Program bone-loss extrapolations
source.publisher: NASA-funded spaceflight medicine research, as reported in science press coverage

notes: Illustrative extrapolation: a ~6-month ISS mission produces roughly 7-11% cumulative hip bone density loss without countermeasures (using ~1.5%/month); a ~30-month Mars round trip, at the same unmitigated rate, could in principle reach 30-60% per NASA-funded research summaries. 30% (the low end) shown here as the conservative estimate. This is why ISS crews perform ~2.5 hours/day of resistive and aerobic exercise (e.g. the Advanced Resistive Exercise Device) as a countermeasure.
